page: Amazon Web Services m7i.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes hyper-threading with 2 threads per core and a 105 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or a GPU, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1747.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU value of 1845.29. However, multi-core and memory-bound performance metrics are relatively weak to poor. The multi-core Geekbench score is 2133.0, and the stress-ng multi-core performance is rated poor at 1895.08. Memory bandwidth is limited, with large-block read-only bandwidth at 13.5 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 14.89 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and AVX-512, though complex workloads like software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations show lower relative performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7i.large offers a low-cost entry point into the dedicated Intel Xeon Gen7 family without the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and moderate single-threaded capabilities, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, text processing, simple background workers, and small-scale application hosting where high multi-core throughput or local storage is not required.
